 18        'react-hooks/rules-of-hooks': 'error',
 19        'react-hooks/exhaustive-deps': 'warn',
 20        '@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars': ['error', { argsIgnorePattern: '^_' }],
 21        '@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports': 'error',
 22        'no-console': ['warn', { allow: ['warn', 'error'] }],

$ npx eslint --print-config ...  ->  @typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion  -- NOT SET --

12 occurrences / 5 files (ripgrep):
  src/components/ui/useFocusTrap.ts:47   const first = items[0]!;
  src/components/ui/useFocusTrap.ts:48   const last  = items[items.length - 1]!;
  src/lib/storage/migrate.test.ts:93,103,113,116   src/components/ui/toastStore.test.ts:25(x2),30
  src/features/review/reviewQueue.test.tsx:95,112  src/features/profile/ProfileContext.test.tsx:16
findings.verifierNote: The lint-config gap is real; the risk narrative around it is not. VERIFIED TRUE: `@typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion` is genuinely not configured — I ran `npx eslint --print-config src/components/ui/useFocusTrap.ts` and the rule resolves to `undefined` (the recommended set only contributes `no-extra-non-null-assertion` and `no-non-null-asserted-optional-chain`). eslint.config.js:17-28 has no entry for it. The count is also exactly right: 12 assertions on 11 lines in 5 files (src/components/ui/useFocusTrap.ts:47,48; src/lib/storage/migrate.test.ts:93,103,113,116; src/components/ui/toastStore.test.ts:25 x2, :30; src/features/review/reviewQueue.test.tsx:95,112; src/features/profile/ProfileContext.test.tsx:16). VERIFIED FALSE — two independent reasons the title's word 'unguarded' and the claim that 'an empty items list is plausible' do not survive a read of the file: (1) src/components/ui/useFocusTrap.ts:45 is `if (items.length === 0) return;`, immediately above the two assertions at lines 47-48. An empty list provably cannot reach them. (2) The assertions are redundant no-ops under this repo's tsconfig. I proved it with the repo's own tsc 6.0.3: with `--strict` alone (matching tsconfig.json, which has no `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`), `const first = items[0]; const t: string = first.tag;` compiles with exit 0; adding `--noUncheckedIndexedAccess` produces `TS18048: 'first' is possibly 'undefined'`. So `items[0]` is already typed `HTMLElement`, and the `!` asserts nothing. That leaves 10 of 12 sites in `*.test.ts(x)` files, where the worst outcome is an opaque 'Cannot read properties of undefined' instead of a clean assertion failure. Nothing here can cause a production incident, which is the spec's own dividing line: `low` is 'worth fixing for hygiene but won't cause incidents'. Amending medium -> low. The forward-looking argument (enable the rule before `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` lands, or 10 new `!` become the path of least resistance) stands and is why this is still worth doing.
findings.reachability: The two production sites are unreachable-when-wrong: useFocusTrap.ts:45 returns before them whenever `items` is empty, and the Tab handler at line 42 only runs on a Tab keypress inside an open dialog. The other 10 sites execute only under Vitest.
findings.blastRadius: 12 assertions / 11 lines / 5 files, of which 10 assertions in 4 files are test-only. Production exposure: 2 assertions in 1 file, both guarded and both no-ops. Enabling the rule as `warn` would surface exactly these 12 and nothing else.
findings.suggestedPatch:
Two-part, both trivial. (1) Add the rule to the `rules` block in eslint.config.js after line 21:

```js
'@typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion': 'warn',
```

(2) Because the production pair is redundant, just delete the two `!` — src/components/ui/useFocusTrap.ts:47-48 become:

```ts
const first = items[0];
const last = items[items.length - 1];
```

This typechecks unchanged today (proved above) and the `items.length === 0` guard at line 45 already establishes the invariant. For the 10 test sites, swap `x!.id` for an explicit `expect(x).toBeDefined()` before the read, or narrow with `if (!x) throw new Error(...)`, so a broken repository read fails with a readable message. RISK: if `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is later enabled (a separate finding), useFocusTrap.ts:47-48 will then need real narrowing rather than the deleted `!` — hoist to `const [first] = items; const last = items.at(-1); if (!first || !last) return;`.

findings.title: useRouteError() is unknown but is narrowed only by `instanceof Error`, so every 404 renders a generic message
findings.description:
`useRouteError()` is declared `(): unknown` (node_modules/react-router/dist/development/lib/hooks.d.ts:723). At runtime it yields one of two shapes: a thrown `Error`, or react-router's `ErrorResponse`. `ErrorResponseImpl` does NOT extend `Error` — it is a plain class (node_modules/react-router/dist/development/lib/router/utils.js:787 `var ErrorResponseImpl = class { status; statusText; data; ... }`). So `error instanceof Error` is definitively false for the whole `ErrorResponse` arm, and the component silently falls to the generic string.

CONCRETE FAILURE: navigate to any unmatched URL (mistyped path, stale bookmark, shared link with a typo). react-router builds `new ErrorResponseImpl(404, 'Not Found', new Error('No route matches URL "/typo"'), true)` (router.js:2742-2750). Because `routeTable` has exactly one top-level route, `getShortCircuitMatches` (router.js:2721 — `routes.length === 1 ? routes[0] : ...`) attaches that error to the root route, whose `errorElement` is this component (src/app/routes.tsx:16). The user therefore gets 'Something went wrong / An unexpected error occurred.' for a 404, and `status`, `statusText` and `data` are all discarded. Note the route table has no `path: '*'` catch-all, so this is the only 404 surface in the app.

react-router exports the discriminator for exactly this: `isRouteErrorResponse(error): error is ErrorResponse` (lib/router/utils.d.ts:958). It is not imported here. Adding it turns `unknown` into a real two-arm narrow and lets the boundary distinguish 'page not found' from 'the app crashed'.

VERIFIED NEGATIVE worth recording: there is NO `(error as Error).message` cast here. A thrown string, number, `null` or plain object falls to the fallback string rather than crashing the boundary. The `unknown` handling is safe, just incomplete.

BLAST RADIUS: every unmatched URL plus every `Response`/`ErrorResponse` thrown from anywhere in the route tree. `src/app/routing.test.tsx` covers `/`, `/book/:id`, `/stats` and back-navigation but never exercises the error path, so this is untested.
findings.verifierNote: Every link in the chain checks out against the actual react-router build in node_modules. src/app/ErrorBoundary.tsx:5-6 is verbatim as reported: `const error = useRouteError();` then `const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'An unexpected error occurred.';`. `ErrorResponseImpl` really is a plain class with no `extends Error` — node_modules/react-router/dist/development/index-react-server.js:805 reads `var ErrorResponseImpl = class { status; statusText; data; error; internal; constructor(status, statusText, data, internal = false) {...} }`, so `instanceof Error` is definitively false for that entire arm. The 404 path is exactly as described: `handleNavigational404` (lib/router/router.js:1211-1214) calls `getInternalRouterError(404, { pathname })`, which returns `new ErrorResponseImpl(status || 500, 'Not Found', new Error('No route matches URL "<path>"'), true)` (router.js ~2735-2750), and then `getShortCircuitMatches(routesToUse)` (router.js:2720) which begins `let route = routes.length === 1 ? routes[0] : ...`. src/app/routes.tsx:12-26 has exactly one top-level route, so the 404 is attached to it, and that route carries `errorElement: <ErrorBoundary />` (routes.tsx:16). Confirmed there is no `path: '*'` catch-all anywhere in routes.tsx, so this component is the app's only 404 surface. Result: every mistyped URL renders 'Something went wrong / An unexpected error occurred.' while `status` (404), `statusText` ('Not Found') and `data` are discarded. The discriminator exists and is exported: `isRouteErrorResponse(error: any): error is ErrorResponse` (index-react-server.d.ts:999, re-exported from 'react-router' at index.d.ts:44) — and react-router's own default boundary uses it at lib/hooks.js:628 (`isRouteErrorResponse(error) ? `${error.status} ${error.statusText}` : error instanceof Error ? error.message : JSON.stringify(error)`), which is precisely the three-arm narrow this component is missing. The discoverer's VERIFIED NEGATIVE also holds: there is no `(error as Error).message` cast here, so a thrown primitive falls to the fallback string rather than crashing the boundary — the `unknown` handling is safe but incomplete, which is the right characterisation. Test coverage confirmed absent: src/app/routing.test.tsx has 6 `it(...)` blocks (library route, book navigation, back button, stats-by-URL, dark theme, unknown-book-id redirect) and none renders the error boundary. Severity `medium` is right — a reachable, user-visible degradation with no crash or data loss.
findings.reachability: Fully reachable with no gating: type any unmatched path into the address bar, follow a stale bookmark, or open a shared link with a typo. Also fires for any `Response`/`ErrorResponse` thrown from anywhere in the route tree.
findings.blastRadius: One component, but it is the single error surface for the entire route tree (6 routes plus the shell) and the only 404 handler in the app. `useRouteError` is imported exactly once, at src/app/ErrorBoundary.tsx:1.

findings.title: routeTable is exported with no RouteObject[] annotation, which disables excess-property checking on the whole route tree
findings.description:
`export const routeTable = [...]` carries no type annotation. Because the array literal is bound to a variable before it reaches `createBrowserRouter` at line 31, its type loses object-literal freshness, and TypeScript's excess-property check never runs on it. A misspelled route key therefore compiles clean and silently produces a route that does nothing.

EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED with this repo's own compiler (node_modules/.bin/tsc, TypeScript 6.0.3) on an isolated probe reproducing react-router's `RouteObject = IndexRouteObject | NonIndexRouteObject` union (lib/router/utils.d.ts:535-562): the identical literal containing `errorELement` compiles with ZERO errors when the const is unannotated, and errors `TS2561: Object literal may only specify known properties, but 'errorELement' does not exist in type 'NonIndexR'. Did you mean to write 'errorElement'?` the moment the annotation is added. All `BaseRouteObject` members are optional, so nothing else catches the typo either.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY: react-router pairs mutually-exclusive spellings that are easy to confuse — `element`/`Component`, `errorElement`/`ErrorBoundary`, `hydrateFallbackElement`/`HydrateFallback`. Writing `ErrorElement` or `Element` compiles today. If `errorElement` (line 16) were typo'd, the app would ship with no error boundary at all and `src/app/routing.test.tsx` would still pass — it covers `/`, `/book/:id`, `/stats` and back-navigation, never the error path.

NOTE ON CATEGORY: `routeTable` is an exported const, not a function. `untyped-public-function` is the closest enum member; the spec's Scope section explicitly lists 'exported value types' under missing/weak annotations. Re-bucket if the aggregate has a better home.

BLAST RADIUS: the entire route tree — six routes, the shell, and the error boundary. Fix shape is a one-word annotation: `export const routeTable: RouteObject[] = [...]`.
findings.evidence:
12: export const routeTable = [
13:   {
14:     path: '/',
15:     element: <AppShell />,
16:     errorElement: <ErrorBoundary />,
17:     children: [
18:       { index: true, element: <LibraryPage /> },
...
31:   const router = useMemo(() => createBrowserRouter(routeTable), []);
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced independently with this repo's own compiler. src/app/routes.tsx:12 is verbatim `export const routeTable = [` with no annotation, and it is bound to a variable before reaching `createBrowserRouter(routeTable)` at routes.tsx:31 — so object-literal freshness is gone and excess-property checking never runs. I built a probe reproducing react-router's union shape and ran node_modules/.bin/tsc (TypeScript 6.0.3) with `--noEmit --ignoreConfig --strict`: the identical literal containing `errorELement` assigned to an UNANNOTATED const produced zero errors, and the same literal assigned to an annotated `R[]` produced `error TS2561: Object literal may only specify known properties, but 'errorELement' does not exist in type 'R'. Did you mean to write 'errorElement'?`. The discoverer's empirical claim is exactly right. The fix is also confirmed viable end-to-end: `createBrowserRouter(routes: RouteObject[], opts?: DOMRouterOpts): Router` (node_modules/react-router/dist/development/lib/dom/lib.d.ts:525) and `type RouteObject` is publicly exported from 'react-router' (index.d.ts:44). The confusable-key argument is verified in node_modules/react-router/dist/development/lib/router/utils.d.ts: `ErrorBoundary?: React.ComponentType | null` at line 515 is documented 'Mutually exclusive with `errorElement`' (line 513), and `errorElement?: React.ReactNode | null` sits at line 520; the same pattern repeats for `HydrateFallback` (525) / `hydrateFallbackElement` (530). Every `BaseRouteObject` member is optional, so nothing else catches a misspelling. Test coverage confirmed absent for the failure mode: src/app/routing.test.tsx has 6 tests and none exercises the error boundary, so a typo'd `errorElement` would ship green. Keeping `medium`: this is not cosmetic — it is a compiler check that is switched off across the whole route tree, which is precisely the spec's medium definition ('erodes confidence and refactor safety but isn't on a critical path'). CATEGORY CAVEAT stands as the discoverer noted: `routeTable` is an exported const, not a function, so `untyped-public-function` is a forced fit; the spec's Scope section does explicitly list 'exported value types' under missing/weak annotations, so I am leaving the category rather than inventing one.
findings.reachability: No present defect — there is no typo in routes.tsx today. The exposure is prospective: any future edit to the route table can introduce a silently-ignored key that compiles clean, and the most damaging variant (misspelled `errorElement`) would remove the app's only error boundary with no test failure.
findings.blastRadius: The whole route tree: 1 top-level route + 6 children + the shell + the error boundary, all in src/app/routes.tsx:12-26. `routeTable` is exported and consumed at routes.tsx:31 and by src/app/routing.test.tsx.
findings.suggestedPatch:
One-line annotation plus a type-only import (the repo enforces `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` at eslint.config.js:21). In src/app/routes.tsx line 2 area add:

```tsx
import type { RouteObject } from 'react-router';
```

and change line 12 to:

```tsx
export const routeTable: RouteObject[] = [
```

This restores excess-property checking on all seven route objects, proved above to catch `errorELement` as TS2561. RISK: minimal — `createBrowserRouter` already declares this exact parameter type (lib/dom/lib.d.ts:525), so the annotation cannot narrow anything the call site did not already require; if the annotation surfaces a pre-existing incompatibility, that is a real defect being revealed, not introduced.

findings.title: Routing test drives an unsummarised book to its detail page and stops one click short of the summary! crash
findings.description: routing.test.tsx is the ONLY test in the repo that mounts the real BookDetail through the router (App.tsx:32-36 -> AppRoutes -> BookDetailPage.tsx:40 -> BookDetail). Its fixture book (lines 12-22) is created with NO summaryId, so useBookRoute.ts:21 resolves summary to undefined and BookDetail receives summary={undefined}. BookDetailProps declares `summary: Summary | undefined` (BookDetail.tsx:119), but the Chat and Quiz buttons are gated ONLY on `!isPreview` (BookDetail.tsx:337) -- isPreview is not passed by BookDetailPage, so it is undefined/falsy and both buttons always render. BookDetail.tsx:534/536 then pass `summary!` into ChatModal/QuizModal, which both declare `summary: Summary` as REQUIRED (ChatModal.tsx:11). The non-null assertion is a lie for every Goodreads-imported (unsummarised) book. ChatModal.tsx:36-38 calls createBookChatSession(book, summary) inside a useEffect with no try/catch; chat.ts:15 forwards it to prompts.ts:61 which dereferences `summary.oneSentenceTakeaway` -> TypeError, rethrown as an AiError from inside a useEffect, which React escalates to the route ErrorBoundary and blanks the app. The test navigates to exactly that screen (line 51) and then asserts ONLY `window.location.pathname` (line 53) -- it never asserts the detail page rendered and never clicks Chat or Quiz. UNTESTED PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR: the entire unsummarised-book detail surface, i.e. the default state of every book a user imports from Goodreads.
findings.verifierNote: Every factual claim checks out, but the severity is a double-count of F002. Verified: the fixture at src/app/routing.test.tsx:12-22 passes no summaryId, so useBookRoute.ts:21 -> summaries.getByBook() (repo.ts:112-114) resolves to undefined and BookDetailPage.tsx:42 hands `summary={undefined}` down; BookDetailPage.tsx:39-53 never passes `isPreview`, so BookDetail.tsx:337 `{!isPreview && (` is true and both buttons render; BookDetail.tsx:534/536 then pass `summary!`. The test at routing.test.tsx:47-54 asserts only `window.location.pathname` on line 53 and never clicks Chat or Quiz. I also confirmed the crash mechanism the description asserts (chat.ts:15 -> prompts.ts:61, and react-router's RenderErrorBoundary at node_modules/react-router/dist/development/lib/hooks.js:645-673 is a real React class error boundary with getDerivedStateFromError + componentDidCatch, so a throw out of ChatModal's useEffect does reach src/app/ErrorBoundary.tsx). What is wrong is the severity: this finding is a *test-coverage gap*, and a missing assertion cannot itself crash anything. The production defect it masks is already filed as F002 (BookDetail.tsx:534/536) and F003 (ChatModal.tsx:11). Rating this Critical triple-counts one bug across the severity table. Downgraded to Medium: it is the repo's only router-integration test and the gap is exactly where the bug lives, which is genuinely worth fixing, but the impact is 'the suite is green on a broken path', not 'users crash'.
findings.reachability: Not directly user-reachable — this is test code. The masked production path is F002's (Goodreads-import a book -> open it -> click Chat). The coverage gap is what let that path ship green.
findings.blastRadius: 1 test file, 6 tests. src/app/routing.test.tsx is the only test in src/ that mounts BookDetail through the real router (App.tsx:34 -> routes.tsx:19 -> BookDetailPage), so no other suite covers the unsummarised-book detail surface either.

findings.title: No test navigates to an unmatched URL, so useRouteError()'s unnarrowed unknown silently turns every 404 into a generic error
findings.description: The suite's only negative-path test covers `/book/does-not-exist` (line 95) -- a URL that DOES match the `book/:id` route and is redirected by useBookRoute.ts:17-19. No test ever visits a URL with no matching route. routes.tsx:12-26 declares no catch-all `path: '*'`, so react-router throws its own 404 object. ErrorBoundary.tsx:5-6 receives it from `useRouteError()`, whose declared return type is `unknown`, and narrows with a single `error instanceof Error` check. react-router 8's ErrorResponseImpl does NOT extend Error, so that branch never taken and every unmatched URL renders the generic fallback string 'An unexpected error occurred.' under the heading 'Something went wrong' instead of a not-found page. This is the permanent-`unknown` pattern: an unknown crossing a boundary, narrowed once, with the residual arm silently swallowed (`isRouteErrorResponse` is the library-provided tag check that is not used). UNTESTED PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR: every typo'd or stale URL a user or a search engine hits.
findings.verifierNote: Every mechanical claim verified — including the load-bearing one about react-router internals — but the impact is a wrong error message, not a failure, so High is a notch too high. CONFIRMED: src/app/routing.test.tsx:94-98 is the suite's only negative-path test and it covers `/book/does-not-exist`, which DOES match `book/:id` (routes.tsx:19) and is redirected by useBookRoute.ts:17-19 — so it exercises the redirect, not the 404. No test in the file visits an unmatched URL. routes.tsx:12-26 declares no catch-all `path: '*'` (read in full). src/app/ErrorBoundary.tsx:5-6 is verbatim as quoted: `useRouteError()` returns `unknown` and is narrowed by a lone `error instanceof Error`, with `isRouteErrorResponse` — the library's own tag check — unused. The key claim checks out in node_modules: react-router 8.3.0's `ErrorResponseImpl` is declared `var ErrorResponseImpl = class {` at node_modules/react-router/dist/development/lib/router/utils.js:787-802, with NO `extends Error` (it merely stores the Error in a `.error` field at line 799 when constructed from one). And the 404 does route to this boundary: router.js:150-154 calls `getShortCircuitMatches(dataRoutes.activeRoutes)` and sets `initialErrors = { [route.id]: error }`, which for a single-root route table resolves to the root route — the one carrying `errorElement: <ErrorBoundary />` at routes.tsx:16. So `error instanceof Error` is provably false and every unmatched URL renders 'Something went wrong / An unexpected error occurred.' WHY MEDIUM: the user-visible outcome is a generic error page instead of a not-found page. No crash, no data loss, no broken flow — the 'Back to library' link at ErrorBoundary.tsx:18-23 still works. Per the spec's scale that is 'erodes confidence... but isn't on a critical path'. It also, like F001, files a test-coverage gap under the severity of the production defect (which lives at ErrorBoundary.tsx:6, not in the test).
findings.reachability: Fully reachable, low consequence: type or follow any URL with no matching route (e.g. /libary, /settings, a stale deep link) -> react-router raises its internal 404 ErrorResponse -> router.js:150-154 assigns it to the root route -> ErrorBoundary.tsx:6's instanceof check fails -> the generic 'An unexpected error occurred.' renders under 'Something went wrong'. Matters more once the Phase 4 GitHub Pages demo is public and stale links exist.
findings.blastRadius: 1 narrowing site (ErrorBoundary.tsx:6) plus the missing test. That single `instanceof Error` check is the app's only error-message surface, so it swallows the detail of every non-Error thrown value, not just 404s.
findings.amendedDescription: The routing suite's only negative-path test (src/app/routing.test.tsx:94-98) covers `/book/does-not-exist`, a URL that DOES match `book/:id` (routes.tsx:19) and is redirected by useBookRoute.ts:17-19. No test ever visits a URL with no matching route, and routes.tsx:12-26 declares no catch-all `path: '*'`, so react-router raises its own 404 and — via getShortCircuitMatches (react-router/dist/development/lib/router/router.js:150-154) — assigns it to the root route's errorElement. src/app/ErrorBoundary.tsx:5-6 receives it from `useRouteError()`, whose declared return type is `unknown`, and narrows with a single `error instanceof Error`. react-router 8.3.0's ErrorResponseImpl (react-router/dist/development/lib/router/utils.js:787) does NOT extend Error, so that branch is never taken and every unmatched URL renders the generic 'An unexpected error occurred.' under 'Something went wrong' instead of a not-found page. This is the permanent-`unknown` pattern: an unknown crossing a boundary, narrowed once, with the residual arm silently swallowed while the library's own tag check, `isRouteErrorResponse`, goes unused. Severity is Medium rather than High: the outcome is a wrong error message on a typo'd or stale URL, not a crash or data loss, and the recovery links still work — but it will be user-visible once the Phase 4 public demo ships.

findings.title: handleAiError is typed total over `unknown` but throws on a null or undefined throwable
findings.description:
`handleAiError: (error: unknown) => string` is the contract three feature modules consume through `useShell()` (BookDetailPage.tsx:15, LibraryPage.tsx:19, ReaderPage.tsx:11) plus `AddBookModal` via its `onAiError` prop. The signature promises totality: hand it ANY value, get a string back. The implementation does not deliver that.

The `unknown` is accepted at the boundary and never narrowed anywhere along the chain. AppShell.tsx:48 forwards it verbatim to `toAiError`, which reads a property off it through `statusOf` (src/lib/ai/errors.ts:39-42): `const status = (error as { status?: unknown }).status;`. That assertion has no null guard, so `toAiError(null)` and `toAiError(undefined)` throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'status')` rather than returning an `AiError`.

CONCRETE FAILURE: every call site is inside a `catch` block — LibraryPage.tsx:80, LibraryPage.tsx:98, AddBookModal.tsx:83. A throw from the error handler escapes the catch, propagates out of the render/event path, and unmounts the route into the root ErrorBoundary — which then (per L08-F02) renders 'An unexpected error occurred.' The failure handler becomes the crash.

REACHABILITY CAVEAT — stated honestly: nothing in `src/` throws a non-object (verified by grep for `throw null|undefined|'|"|{|<digit>` and bare `reject()` across src/ — zero hits), and `src/lib/ai/*` already wraps its throws in `toAiError`, so the common paths arrive as `AiError` and short-circuit at errors.ts:46. The trigger is a non-object rejection surfacing from `@google/genai` or `fetch`. Possible, not proven — hence medium, not high.

CORRECT SHAPE: narrow at the boundary. Either `statusOf` guards `typeof error === 'object' && error !== null` before the property read, or `handleAiError` narrows before forwarding. The permanent un-narrowed `unknown` is what lets the lie through.

BLAST RADIUS: four call sites, all in catch blocks, all on AI-feature paths.
findings.verifierNote: The crash is real and I proved it, but the finding is anchored to the wrong file, line and category, and undercounts the blast radius by 4x. Amending all three. WHAT IS TRUE: src/lib/ai/errors.ts:39-42 is `function statusOf(error: unknown): number | undefined { const status = (error as { status?: unknown }).status; return typeof status === 'number' ? status : undefined; }` — an unguarded property read through a bare assertion. I ran the exact logic under node: `statusOf(null)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'status')` and `statusOf(undefined)` throws the undefined equivalent; string and number inputs return undefined harmlessly. `toAiError` reaches it: for `error = null`, errors.ts:46 (`instanceof AiError`) is false, errors.ts:48 gives `message = String(null) = 'null'`, none of the `quota`/`safety`/`SyntaxError`/`TypeError` branches at errors.ts:53-56 match, so control falls to errors.ts:58 `const status = statusOf(error);` and throws. So the function documented at errors.ts:44 as 'Normalises anything thrown by the Gemini SDK or fetch into an AiError' throws on two of the values in its own declared `unknown` domain — a genuine lying type. src/lib/ai/errors.test.ts covers AiError passthrough, status codes, quota, safety, TypeError-fetch and SyntaxError; it never passes null or undefined. WHAT IS WRONG: the finding is filed against src/app/ShellContext.ts:9 under `unknown-misuse`, but `handleAiError: (error: unknown) => string` is the CORRECT type for a catch-clause value — `unknown` is exactly what the spec says it should be there, and AppShell.tsx:47-56 forwards it faithfully. The defect lives entirely in the assertion at errors.ts:40, so the category is `type-assertion-as-T` and the anchor is src/lib/ai/errors.ts:40. BLAST RADIUS IS 4x LARGER than the claimed 'four call sites': `toAiError` is called from 16 places — 9 inside `src/lib/ai` catch blocks (client.ts:26, chat.ts:18, chat.ts:37, recommend.ts:41, quiz.ts:19, summarize.ts:56, summarize.ts:77, summarize.ts:101, tts.ts:32) and 7 in UI code (AppShell.tsx:48, BookDetail.tsx:169, BookDetail.tsx:189, QuizModal.tsx:65, ChatModal.tsx:72, EReader.tsx:213, ApiKeyDialog.tsx:33). Severity stays `medium`: the discoverer's reachability caveat was honest and correct — I re-checked and nothing in src/ throws a non-object, and every `src/lib/ai/*` path pre-wraps into `AiError` which short-circuits at errors.ts:46, so triggering this needs a non-object rejection escaping @google/genai or fetch. Larger radius but same unproven trigger nets out at medium.
findings.reachability: Not demonstrably reachable from src/ alone. All 9 `src/lib/ai` sites wrap their own throws, so values arriving at `toAiError` are already `AiError` and return at errors.ts:46. The trigger requires @google/genai or the platform to reject with `null`/`undefined`; `fetch` never does, and @google/genai throws Error subclasses. If it did occur, the consequence is severe out of proportion to the cause: every UI call site is inside a `catch` (e.g. AddBookModal.tsx:81-83, LibraryPage.tsx:79-80 and :97-98, QuizModal.tsx:63-65), so the error handler's own throw escapes the catch, unwinds the render/event path and drops the route into the root ErrorBoundary — which then renders the generic message per F054. The failure handler becomes the failure.
findings.blastRadius: 16 `toAiError` call sites across 12 files (9 in src/lib/ai, 7 in UI), plus the 4 `handleAiError`/`onAiError` consumers the discoverer counted (ShellContext.ts:9, AppShell.tsx:47/196, LibraryPage.tsx:19/80/98, AddBookModal.tsx:23/83). Every AI feature in the app funnels through this one function.

findings.title: BookDetail reads the Summary's takeaway while BookCard reads the denormalised copy, and they visibly disagree
findings.description: The same fact is stored twice with different types and no invariant tying them: `Summary.oneSentenceTakeaway` is required `string` (types.ts:57) and `Book.oneSentenceTakeaway` is optional `string` (types.ts:48). BookDetail line 452 renders the Summary copy; `BookCard.tsx:89` renders the Book copy with a falsy fallback (`book.oneSentenceTakeaway ? ... : 'Not summarised yet'`). Nothing keeps them in sync: `book.oneSentenceTakeaway` is written ONLY at creation time (`AddBookModal.tsx:72`, `LibraryPage.tsx:92`), and `saveSummary` (useLibrary.tsx:78-88) syncs only `book.summaryId` back onto the book - never the takeaway. WHAT THE USER SEES: a book whose stored `oneSentenceTakeaway` is `''` (migrate.ts:125 writes exactly that for legacy records, and any imported backup can carry it) has a real Summary with `summaryId` set, yet its BookCard says 'Not summarised yet' in the library while opening it shows the genuine takeaway quoted in the orange panel - the library and the detail view contradict each other about the same book. The optional-vs-required typing is what permits it: the compiler cannot express 'if `summaryId` is set then `oneSentenceTakeaway` is a non-empty string'. FIX SHAPE: fold the denormalised fields into the tagged union proposed in L11-F02 so they can only be absent together, and have `saveSummary` write the takeaway back onto the Book whenever the Summary changes. Note the denormalisation itself is deliberate (CLAUDE.md) and should be kept - only the sync and the typing need fixing.
findings.verifierNote: The contradiction is real and I confirm it, but the mechanism the discoverer identified is the wrong one and the true mechanism is deterministic rather than conditional — amending the description, keeping the severity. VERIFIED: `Summary.oneSentenceTakeaway` is required `string` (src/types.ts:57) while `Book.oneSentenceTakeaway` is optional `string` (src/types.ts:48). src/components/BookDetail.tsx:452 renders the Summary copy (`{summary ? `"${summary.oneSentenceTakeaway}"` : ''}`) and src/components/BookCard.tsx:89 renders the Book copy with a falsy fallback (`{book.oneSentenceTakeaway ? `"${book.oneSentenceTakeaway}"` : 'Not summarised yet'}`) — both verbatim. An exhaustive grep for `oneSentenceTakeaway` confirms `book.oneSentenceTakeaway` has exactly TWO writers, both at creation time: src/components/AddBookModal.tsx:72 and src/features/library/LibraryPage.tsx:92. `saveSummary` (src/features/library/useLibrary.tsx:78-88) syncs only `summaryId` and never the takeaway — and per this audit's established baseline its backfill at lines 82-83 is dead code anyway. CORRECTION TO THE MECHANISM: the discoverer blamed src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:125, but that line writes the SUMMARY's takeaway (`oneSentenceTakeaway: legacy.oneSentenceTakeaway ?? ''`), not the Book's. The actual violation is at src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:105-119, where `books.create({...})` sets `summaryId` (line 117) but OMITS `oneSentenceTakeaway` entirely — the field is not in the object literal at all. It compiles because the field is optional. So `book.oneSentenceTakeaway` is `undefined` for 100% of migrated legacy books, not just for the subset whose legacy takeaway was empty. Every legacy user therefore sees 'Not summarised yet' on every card in their library while opening any of those books shows the genuine takeaway in the orange panel — the two views contradict each other about every migrated book, deterministically. That is strictly stronger than the reported ''-valued case and matches this audit's already-established correction that the invariant is violated for real at migrate.ts:105-119. The type angle is legitimate and not a pattern-match: `oneSentenceTakeaway?` being optional while `summaryId?` is independently optional is exactly what lets migrate.ts construct the impossible state and compile. Severity stays `medium` — a durable, deterministic, user-visible inconsistency, but cosmetic in consequence (no crash, no data loss).
findings.reachability: Deterministic on the legacy-migration path, which every pre-IndexedDB user hits exactly once. `migrateLegacyData` (src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:80) runs when `booksum_library_*` keys exist and the `booksum.migratedAt` marker is unset (lines 81-84); every book it creates gets `summaryId` but no `oneSentenceTakeaway`. Books added via AddBookModal or the recommendation preview are unaffected (both writers set the field). Goodreads-imported books are self-consistent — useLibrary.tsx:150-160 sets neither `summaryId` nor the takeaway — and I confirmed BookDetail offers no 'summarise this existing book' action (BookDetail.tsx:183 bails with `if (!summary) return`), so they cannot drift into the inconsistent state.
findings.blastRadius: One denormalised field, 2 writers (AddBookModal.tsx:72, LibraryPage.tsx:92) and 3 readers (BookCard.tsx:89 reads the Book copy; BookDetail.tsx:452 and DailyWisdomModal.tsx:60 read the Summary copy). Affects every book row rendered in the library grid and in StatsView for migrated profiles. src/lib/storage/migrate.test.ts exists but asserts on the Summary side, not on `book.oneSentenceTakeaway`.

findings.title: `pages[currentPage]` is typed `string` but can be `undefined`, crashing the reader on a whitespace-only deep dive
findings.description:
`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off, so `pages[currentPage]` (line 395) is typed `string` and satisfies `RenderFormattedContent`'s `content: string` prop (line 53) even when the index is out of range. The declared contract - `pages` is a non-empty `string[]` and `currentPage` is always in range - is enforced by nothing. PRODUCER CHAIN for an empty `pages`: `generateDetailedSummary` returns `text || 'Failed to generate detailed summary.'` (summarize.ts:97) - it guards the empty string but NOT a whitespace-only stream. A model response of `'

  '` is truthy, so it is stored as `detailedSummary`; EReader's guard on line 183 (`!summary?.detailedSummary`) passes it through; lines 185-188 then `.split(/(?=## )/g).map(trim).filter(Boolean)` reduce it to `[]`. Now `pages.length === 0`, `pages[0]` is `undefined`, and `content.split('
')` on line 58 throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')` - the reader route dies into the error boundary. The same empty-`pages` state also makes line 457 compute `((0 + 1) / 0) * 100 = Infinity`, emitting `style={{ width: 'Infinity%' }}`, and line 461 renders the literal text 'Infinity% Complete'. SECOND TRIGGER, same root: `currentPage` is never clamped against `pages.length`, so any shrink of the memo while the reader is mounted leaves the index dangling. BLAST RADIUS: the /book/:id/read route; the failure is durable because the bad `detailedSummary` is persisted, so re-opening the reader crashes again until the summary is regenerated. FIX SHAPE: enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` (this file and the two others in the lot would need ~7 sites touched, see L11-F08), and make the non-emptiness real - have the memo fall back to the placeholder page when `sections` is empty, and clamp `currentPage` into range.
findings.verifierNote:
Pattern confirmed exactly, reachability narrower than claimed, and the second trigger is refuted. CONFIRMED: EReader.tsx:395 passes `pages[currentPage]` into `content: string` (declared at line 53) which is dereferenced at line 58 `content.split('
')`; the memo at 182-190 can return `[]`; tsconfig.json:8 sets `strict: true` with no `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and no `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` (both absent from the file), so `pages[currentPage]` types as a definite `string`. I reproduced the full chain in node: `'

  '` passes the truthy guard at line 183, `.split(/(?=## )/g).map(trim).filter(Boolean)` yields `[]`, `pages[0]` is `undefined`, and `content.split` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')`; the progress bar computes `Infinity` (line 457) and line 461 renders 'Infinity% Complete'. The producer note is off by two lines — the fallback is summarize.ts:99 (`return text || 'Failed to generate detailed summary.'`), not :97 — but the point stands: it screens the empty string, not a whitespace-only stream. REFUTED SUB-CLAIM: 'any shrink of the memo while the reader is mounted leaves the index dangling'. `pages` depends only on `summary?.detailedSummary` (line 190) and ReaderPage.tsx:9 never takes `setSummary`, while useBookRoute.ts:21 sets the summary once per book — the reader cannot shrink its own page list mid-session. AMENDED TO MEDIUM: the only live trigger requires Gemini to stream content that is non-empty but entirely whitespace, a narrow model-output edge rather than a routinely-exercised path. The type weakness and the trivial fix are real; the crash probability does not clear the 'critical business path / routinely exercised' bar for high.
findings.reachability: Only via a Gemini stream whose accumulated text is non-empty but whitespace-only: BookDetail.tsx:184 stores it, BookDetailPage.tsx:46 persists it via saveSummary, then /book/:id/read mounts EReader and the render throws into the error boundary. Durable once persisted — reopening the reader crashes again until the summary is regenerated, and there is no regenerate action (BookDetail.tsx:176 short-circuits when detailedSummary exists).
findings.blastRadius: Local: `pages` is used at EReader.tsx:219, 395, 405, 457, 461, 468 within one component; one mount site (ReaderPage.tsx:23). Enabling noUncheckedIndexedAccess repo-wide is the broad-radius variant of the same fix.
findings.amendedDescription: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off (tsconfig.json:2-18 sets `strict: true` and nothing more), so `pages[currentPage]` at EReader.tsx:395 types as a definite `string` and satisfies `RenderFormattedContent`'s `content: string` (line 53) even when the index is out of range. The memo at lines 182-190 can genuinely return `[]`: `generateDetailedSummary` guards only the empty string (`return text || 'Failed to generate detailed summary.'`, summarize.ts:99), so a whitespace-only stream is stored as `detailedSummary`, passes the truthy check at line 183, and is reduced to `[]` by `.split(/(?=## )/g).map(trim).filter(Boolean)`. Verified by execution: `pages[0]` is then `undefined` and `content.split('\n')` at line 58 throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')`, killing the /book/:id/read route into the error boundary; line 457 emits `width: 'Infinity%'` and line 461 renders 'Infinity% Complete'. The failure is durable because the bad `detailedSummary` is persisted. NOTE: the originally claimed second trigger — `currentPage` dangling after the memo shrinks mid-session — is not reachable; `pages` depends only on `summary?.detailedSummary` (line 190) and ReaderPage.tsx:9 never mutates the summary. findings.title: `correctAnswerIndex` is used as an index into `options` with no bounds relationship in the type; an out-of-range index silently makes the quiz unwinnable
findings.description: `QuizQuestion` (types.ts:105-110) models `options: string[]` and `correctAnswerIndex: number` as two independent fields — nothing in the type ties the index to the array's bounds, and nothing validates it (see L12-F03 for the producer). QuizModal renders correctness by comparing the rendered option's position to that index (line 183) and scores by the same comparison (line 78). Failure scenario: the model returns `options: ['A','B','C']` with `correctAnswerIndex: 3` (schema only *describes* "Index (0-3)" and "4 possible answers"). `isCorrect` is then false for every rendered option — no green highlight appears, whichever answer the user picks is styled as wrong, `setScore` is never called, and the finish screen reports `Math.round((0 / n) * 100)` = "0%" with "You answered 0 out of 3 correctly!". The app looks broken and blames the user. Note this is exactly the case `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is designed to expose: with that flag off, an expression like `options[correctAnswerIndex]` is typed as a definite `string` even though it is `undefined` at runtime. Fix shape: validate the index at the boundary and drop or repair malformed questions; longer term, a non-empty-tuple/branded index type or an `{ options, correctAnswer: string }` shape removes the class of bug entirely.
findings.verifierNote: Pattern and failure scenario confirmed; severity lowered because this is the transient twin of F016. VERIFIED at current lines: types.ts:105-110 models `options: string[]` and `correctAnswerIndex: number` as independent fields with no bounds relationship; QuizModal.tsx:183 `const isCorrect = idx === questions[currentQuestionIndex].correctAnswerIndex` drives every option's styling (189-220), line 78 scores by the same comparison, line 93 computes the percentage, line 182 maps the options. With an out-of-range index (or the classic 1-based-index model failure) `isCorrect` is false for every rendered option: no green highlight (190-191, 219), whichever option the user picks is styled wrong (192-193), `setScore` never fires, and lines 146-149 report '0%' / 'You answered 0 out of N correctly!'. AMENDED TO MEDIUM: this is the same root cause as F016 (unvalidated Gemini output, quiz.ts:16) at a different consumer, and F017's INDEPENDENT impact is confined to one modal session — nothing is persisted by lines 78/93/182/183; the durable harm belongs to F016's write at lines 52-61, which already carries high. Rating both at high double-counts one boundary defect. Minor inaccuracy in the description: the `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` remark cites `options[correctAnswerIndex]`, an expression QuizModal never evaluates — it only compares `idx === correctAnswerIndex`, so that flag would not have caught this particular site.
findings.reachability: Same entry as F016 — open a summarised book, click 'Quiz' — but the visible effect here (an unwinnable, always-0% quiz) lasts only as long as the modal is open. Requires the model to return an index outside `[0, options.length)`, which the schema at schemas.ts:69-72 does not prevent.
findings.blastRadius: Four expressions inside one component (QuizModal.tsx:78, 93, 182, 183), one modal session, no persistence. The shared `QuizQuestion` type (types.ts:105-110) has 3 referencing modules (quiz.ts:6, QuizModal.tsx:4, types.ts), and the identical unbounded-index shape is mirrored on `ReviewCard` (types.ts:88-89).
findings.suggestedPatch: No separate patch needed — the boundary guard in F016's `suggestedPatch` (src/lib/ai/quiz.ts:16-17, dropping questions where `Number.isInteger(correctAnswerIndex) && correctAnswerIndex >= 0 && correctAnswerIndex < options.length` fails) fixes this consumer too, because `questions` at QuizModal.tsx:45 is set from the same return value. Land F016's fix and re-verify this one. If a defence-in-depth change is wanted in the component, make the empty state honest rather than adding a cast: QuizModal.tsx:45 `setQuestions(quizData)` unchanged, relying on the existing 'Could not generate quiz.' branch at lines 125-137 which already handles a zero-length list. Risk: none; the only behaviour change is fewer, valid questions instead of an unwinnable one.
findings.amendedDescription: `QuizQuestion` (types.ts:105-110) models `options: string[]` and `correctAnswerIndex: number` as two independent fields — nothing in the type ties the index to the array's bounds, and nothing validates it (the producer is quiz.ts:16, see F016). QuizModal renders correctness by comparing the rendered option's position to that index (QuizModal.tsx:183) and scores by the same comparison (line 78). Failure scenario: the model returns `options: ['A','B','C']` with `correctAnswerIndex: 3`, or 1-based indices, since schemas.ts:69-72 only *describes* 'Index (0-3)' and 'Array of 4 possible answers' in prose. `isCorrect` is then false for every rendered option — no green highlight (lines 190-191, 219), whichever answer the user picks is styled wrong (192-193), `setScore` never fires, and the finish screen reports '0%' and 'You answered 0 out of N correctly!' (lines 146-149). The app looks broken and blames the user. SCOPE: this is the transient face of the same boundary defect as F016 — nothing here is persisted (the durable write is QuizModal.tsx:52-61), so the harm ends when the modal closes, which is why this is medium while F016 stays high. Correction to the original note: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` would NOT have caught this site — QuizModal never evaluates `options[correctAnswerIndex]`, it only compares `idx === correctAnswerIndex`. Fix shape: validate the index at the `generateBookQuiz` boundary (fixing both consumers at once); longer term an `{ options, correctAnswer: string }` shape removes the class of bug entirely.

findings.title: `Book.rating: number` conflates "unrated" with "rated 0", so the average-rating stat is silently wrong for imported libraries
findings.description: `Book.rating` is a required `number` (types.ts:36) with no representation for "not rated". The Goodreads importer therefore substitutes a sentinel: `rating: Number.isFinite(rating) ? rating : 0` (goodreads.ts:111). StatsView then averages every Finished book's rating unconditionally (line 20), so each unrated import drags the mean toward zero — a user who imports 200 Goodreads books and rated 10 of them sees "Avg. Rating 0.2" presented as a fact about their taste. The type system cannot catch it because `0` is a perfectly good `number`. BookCard has the mirrored symptom, rendering `{book.rating}/5` for every Finished book (BookCard.tsx:100), so unrated imports display an authoritative-looking "0/5". Secondary weakness on the same lines: the ternary makes `avgRating` an accidental `string | number` union (`.toFixed(1)` returns `string`, the empty-library branch returns the number `0`), which is why `StatCard.value` had to be widened to `string | number` (line 197) — the display type now accepts anything numeric-or-textual and no longer documents what a stat card shows. Fix shape: make the domain explicit — `rating?: number` (or a branded `Rating` 1..5 with an explicit unrated state) so `reduce` cannot silently include sentinels, and return a single formatted `string` from the memo. Blast radius: StatsView's headline stat plus every BookCard rating badge.
findings.verifierNote: Pattern and data flow confirmed on every cited line. types.ts:36 `rating: number` is required with no 'unrated' representation; goodreads.ts:111 substitutes the sentinel `rating: Number.isFinite(rating) ? rating : 0` (Goodreads exports write 0 for unrated); goodreads.ts:74-76 `toStatus` maps shelf 'read' -> 'Finished', so read-but-unrated rows land in exactly the set StatsView averages. StatsView.tsx:20 reduces `b.rating` over all Finished books with no filter; BookCard.tsx:100 renders `{book.rating}/5` for every Finished book. Secondary claim also holds: StatsView.tsx:18-21 yields `string | number` (`.toFixed(1)` vs the literal `0`), which is why StatCard.value is widened to `string | number` at StatsView.tsx:197. One more consequence the discovery missed, which strengthens it: BookDetail.tsx:215 does `rating: newStatus === 'Finished' ? book.rating || 5 : book.rating`, so marking an unrated import Finished silently fabricates a 5-star rating out of the sentinel. Severity stays medium (wrong displayed data, no crash). Category amended: this is not two same-typed domain concepts being swapped (the branded-type definition) but a missing 'unrated' state, so discriminated-union-opportunity is the accurate bucket and keeps the report's branded-type section honest.
findings.reachability: Import a Goodreads CSV containing read-but-unrated rows (the default for most large exports) -> the Stats headline 'Avg. Rating' is dragged toward 0 and every such book's card shows '0/5'. Marking any of them Finished from BookDetail.tsx:215 converts the sentinel into a fabricated 5.

findings.title: `querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>` is an unchecked assertion over a runtime selector string in the app's shared focus trap
findings.description: `querySelectorAll<E extends Element>(selectors: string): NodeListOf<E>` does not validate `E` against the selector — supplying `HTMLElement` is an assertion, indistinguishable in safety from `as HTMLElement[]`, over a selector string the compiler never parses. Two of the six clauses in `FOCUSABLE` (line 5) — `a[href]` and `[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])` — match non-HTML elements: an `<a>` inside inline SVG is an `SVGAElement`, and any SVG node carrying `tabindex` matches too. The codebase renders inline SVG in every dialog (lucide-react icons inside the close buttons of Dialog.tsx:46, QuizModal.tsx:171, ChatModal.tsx:120, DailyWisdomModal.tsx:44), so the selector runs against SVG content on every open. The assertion also claims nothing about *visibility*: `display:none`/`visibility:hidden`/`inert` controls match the selector, so `focusable()[0]?.focus()` (line 26) can be a silent no-op on a hidden first control, and the Tab wrap-around at lines 51-57 then compares `document.activeElement` against elements that can never hold focus — the trap stops wrapping and Tab escapes the modal to the page behind it, which is the accessibility guarantee the hook exists to provide. Fix shape: keep the query as `Element`, then narrow with a real guard (`instanceof HTMLElement` plus an offsetParent/`checkVisibility()` filter) so the array type is earned rather than asserted. Blast radius: this is the single shared trap for every modal surface in the app — Dialog (used by AddBookModal.tsx:100, ApiKeyDialog.tsx:38 and ConfirmDialog.tsx:39), plus ChatModal.tsx:34, QuizModal.tsx:31 and DailyWisdomModal.tsx:22 which call it directly. Related: the hook's `{ active: boolean }` parameter encodes no notion of a trap *stack*, and both effects register on `document`, so two simultaneously-active traps both handle the same Escape/Tab (line 38's `stopPropagation` does not stop sibling listeners on the same node — that would need `stopImmediatePropagation`). CLAUDE.md documents "never leave two `aria-modal` dialogs open at once" as a convention; the types provide no enforcement of it.
findings.verifierNote: Pattern confirmed at useFocusTrap.ts:18 - `querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(FOCUSABLE)` is an unchecked generic assertion; the compiler never parses the selector at :5. Half the discovery rationale is wrong: grep for `<a ` across src/**/*.tsx returns ZERO inline anchors and there is no `tabIndex` attribute anywhere in the app, so no SVG node can match `a[href]` or `[tabindex]` and the SVGAElement scenario is unreachable. The visibility half is real, and I found the concrete site: AddBookModal.tsx:229-235 renders `<input type="file" className="hidden">` (display:none) inside a Dialog, and in upload mode with no file chosen the submit button at :262-266 is `disabled` and therefore excluded by `button:not([disabled])`. The hidden input is then the LAST entry in `focusable()`, so `last` at useFocusTrap.ts:48 can never equal `document.activeElement`, the forward-Tab wrap at :54-57 never fires, and Tab escapes the aria-modal dialog - the exact guarantee the hook exists to provide. Severity stays medium (accessibility degradation, no crash). The two `!` at :47-48 are guarded by `if (items.length === 0) return;` at :45, consistent with earlier batches.
findings.reachability: Add book -> 'Upload PDF' tab -> Tab forward past the last visible control: focus leaves the modal instead of wrapping, because the disabled submit is filtered out and the display:none file input is last. Same shape in the Goodreads tab (GoodreadsImport.tsx:64-70 hidden input) whenever the import button at :98 is disabled.
findings.blastRadius: Single shared trap for every modal surface: Dialog.tsx:19 (AddBookModal.tsx:100, ApiKeyDialog, ConfirmDialog.tsx:39) plus ChatModal, QuizModal and DailyWisdomModal calling it directly - 6 surfaces, 1 with a proven live failure.
findings.suggestedPatch: useFocusTrap.ts:17-20 -> `() => Array.from(panelRef.current?.querySelectorAll(FOCUSABLE) ?? []).filter((el): el is HTMLElement => el instanceof HTMLElement && el.offsetParent !== null)`. Risk: `offsetParent` is null for `position: fixed` elements, so if a future panel uses a fixed-position control prefer `el.checkVisibility()` with an offsetParent fallback.
findings.amendedDescription: `querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>` at useFocusTrap.ts:18 is an assertion, not a check - the compiler never validates the selector at :5 - and it asserts nothing about visibility. Correction to the discovery rationale: the app renders no inline `<a>` and no `tabindex` attribute, so the SVGAElement mismatch is not reachable. The live defect is hidden controls: AddBookModal.tsx:229 renders a display:none file input inside the Dialog and its submit button is disabled at :264-266, so that hidden input becomes the last focusable, `active === last` at useFocusTrap.ts:54 never holds, and Tab escapes the modal.

findings.title: The only CSV fixture is a canonical Goodreads header, so the parser's silent-coercion path for foreign CSVs is untested
findings.description: The suite's single CSV literal (lines 9-13) carries a perfect Goodreads header, so parseGoodreadsCsv is only ever exercised on input it was designed for. The parser resolves columns via `header.indexOf(name)` (goodreads.ts:82-90) and `cell(index)` returns '' when index === -1 (goodreads.ts:96), so a foreign CSV that merely has a `title` column parses as a clean success: `author` silently becomes 'Unknown' (goodreads.ts:109), `toStatus('')` returns 'Want to Read' for every row (goodreads.ts:74-76), rating collapses to 0 (line 111), isbn13 to undefined, and `skipped` stays 0. The declared return type `GoodreadsRow[]` with `status: BookStatus` claims validated domain data that the parser never validated -- the type is fiction for any non-Goodreads file. GoodreadsImport.tsx:85-90 then reports 'N books found / 0 finished, N to read' with no warning, and useLibrary.tsx:150-160 lands all N. No test in this file (or in lib/goodreads.test.ts's sibling scope) feeds a CSV with a Title column but no Author/Exclusive Shelf column. UNTESTED PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR: a Calibre/StoryGraph/LibraryThing export dumping thousands of books authored 'Unknown', all marked 'Want to Read', behind a clean-looking preview.

findings.verifierNote: The coverage gap is real and I reproduced the untested behaviour, but two things need correcting: the claim about the sibling test file, and the severity. VERIFIED: goodreadsImport.test.tsx:9-13 is exactly as quoted and is the only CSV literal in that file; all four tests (lines 42, 63, 80, 99) feed either that canonical fixture or hand-built row objects (101-106), never a foreign header. I ran `parseGoodreadsCsv` on a StoryGraph/Calibre-shaped header (`Title,Authors,Read Status,Star Rating`) and got `{rows: [{title:'Dune', author:'Unknown', status:'Want to Read', rating:0}, ...], skipped: 0}` — a clean-looking success, exactly the silent-coercion path described, via goodreads.ts:83 `header.indexOf(name)` -> -1, goodreads.ts:96 `cell(-1)` -> '', then 109/110/111. CORRECTION: 'no test in this file (or in lib/goodreads.test.ts's sibling scope) feeds a CSV with a Title column but no Author/Exclusive Shelf column' overstates the gap — goodreads.test.ts:66-70 does test a reduced 3-column header, :72-75 tests reordered columns, and :77-80 tests the 'Unknown' author fallback (via an empty cell, not a missing column). What is genuinely untested is the precise combination 'title present, author AND exclusive shelf both absent' that yields all-defaults with `skipped: 0`. AMENDED TO MEDIUM: this is a test-coverage gap, not a production defect at the cited file:line — the production defect is F019 (same root cause, same parser), already rated high. Rating the test gap high as well double-counts.

The uncovered branch is goodreads.ts:96 `index >= 0 ? ... : ''` for the author and shelf columns specifically.
findings.amendedDescription: The only CSV fixture in goodreadsImport.test.tsx (lines 9-13) is a canonical Goodreads header, so every test in that file (42, 63, 80, 99) exercises `parseGoodreadsCsv` only on input it was designed for. The uncovered branch is goodreads.ts:96 `cell(index)` returning '' when `columnOf` yields -1 (goodreads.ts:83): a CSV that has a `title` column but neither `author` nor `exclusive shelf` parses as a clean success — verified by execution on a StoryGraph/Calibre-shaped header (`Title,Authors,Read Status,Star Rating`), which produced rows with `author: 'Unknown'` (goodreads.ts:109), `status: 'Want to Read'` (goodreads.ts:75,110), `rating: 0` (goodreads.ts:111) and `skipped: 0`. The sibling suite narrows but does not close the gap: goodreads.test.ts:66-70 covers a reduced 3-column header, :72-75 covers reordered columns and :77-80 covers the 'Unknown' author fallback via an empty cell — none covers a missing author/shelf COLUMN. Untested production behaviour: a Calibre/StoryGraph/LibraryThing export dumping thousands of books authored 'Unknown', all 'Want to Read', behind a preview that reports success (GoodreadsImport.tsx:84-91). findings.title: localStorage recommendation cache is cast to a concrete shape and rendered without validation
findings.description: `JSON.parse(cached) as { at: number; items: Recommendation[] }` is a pure assertion over external, persistent, user-writable storage. The value flows unchecked into `setRecommendations(parsed.items)` and then into RecommendationCarousel.tsx:79 `recommendations.map(...)` and `rec.title` / `rec.author` / `rec.description` / `rec.coverUrl`. The try/catch on line 39 only covers `JSON.parse`, i.e. syntax errors -- a syntactically valid but wrong-shaped value passes the assertion, and the resulting failure happens later during the carousel's render, outside the catch, so the self-healing `localStorage.removeItem` on line 40 never runs. Concrete failure: a stored `{"at":,"items":"abc"}` satisfies the `parsed.items?.length` truthiness test (string length 3) and then throws `TypeError: recommendations.map is not a function` from the error boundary -- on every load, permanently, because the poison stays in localStorage. Milder always-live version: entries missing `coverUrl` render `` (React drops the attribute, so `onError` and the placeholder fallback on line 94 may never fire) and entries missing `title` produce `key={undefined}`. Reachability: the app is the only writer today, but a shared origin makes localStorage non-exclusive -- the planned Phase 4 GitHub Pages demo puts BookSum on `.github.io`, one origin shared with every other Pages site under that account -- and any future change to `Recommendation` leaves 24h of stale-shaped caches that still pass the TTL check. Correct behaviour: validate the parsed object (array check plus per-item field check) and drop the cache when it fails, the way ProfileView.tsx:119 at least array-checks its import.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed at LibraryPage.tsx:35: `const parsed = JSON.parse(cached) as { at: number; items: Recommendation[] };` - a bare assertion over localStorage, with the try/catch at :34-41 covering only JSON.parse, so a syntactically valid but wrong-shaped value passes and the self-healing removeItem at :40 never runs. The value flows to setRecommendations(:37) -> RecommendationCarousel `recommendations.map` (:79) and `rec.coverUrl`/`rec.title`/`rec.author` (:91-104). Two refinements from tracing the producer. (a) The app itself cannot write a non-array `items`: recommend.ts:34-39 always returns the result of `.map`, and a non-array `data.recommendations` throws inside recommend.ts's own try and is converted by toAiError - so the `items:"abc"` crash needs a foreign same-origin writer, devtools, or a future `Recommendation` shape change leaving 24h of stale caches. (b) The field-level variant IS live today: recommend.ts:35-36 spreads model output verbatim (`...rec`), so a response missing `title` yields `key={undefined}` and a missing `description` renders blank, then gets cached. Worth adding: the TTL test at :36 is `Date.now() - parsed.at < RECS_TTL_MS`, which is also true for any FUTURE `at`, so a poisoned entry with a forward timestamp never expires. Medium is right - localStorage ingress, no app-writable crash path today.
findings.reachability: Every load of the default route with a cached entry. The crash variant needs an external writer or a post-refactor shape change; the field-drift variant only needs one malformed model response to have been cached by :74-77.
findings.blastRadius: 1 read site (LibraryPage.tsx:32-42) feeding 1 component (RecommendationCarousel, 4 field reads), on the app's default route.
findings.suggestedPatch: Guard next to the parse: `const isRec = (v: unknown): v is Recommendation => !!v && typeof v === 'object' && typeof (v as Recommendation).title === 'string' && typeof (v as Recommendation).author === 'string';` then `const age = Date.now() - parsed?.at; if (typeof parsed?.at === 'number' && age >= 0 && age < RECS_TTL_MS && Array.isArray(parsed.items) && parsed.items.every(isRec)) setRecommendations(parsed.items); else localStorage.removeItem(key);`. Risk: stricter validation drops existing caches once on upgrade, which is the intended behaviour.

findings.title: LibraryPage renders the zero-books empty state during the initial load because it never reads `isLoading`
findings.description: Consumer-side manifestation of L09-F03, on the app's default route. Line 18 destructures only `{ books, addBook, getSummary }` -- `isLoading` is available on the same object and is simply not taken -- so `filteredBooks.length > 0 ? grid : emptyState` treats the loading `[]` as 'this user has no books'. App.tsx:12 gates on `useProfile().isLoading`, not on the library's, so `LibraryProvider` mounts with a settled profile while `books` is still `[]` and `isLoading` is still `true`. The first paint of `/` for a user with 500 imported books is therefore 'Your library is quiet' plus an 'Add Your First Book' button, for the duration of the IndexedDB open + index read. The same array also drives `categories` (line 65), so the topic filter row is empty in that window. This is only possible because the producer's type does not tag its states; the fix here is to consume the tag (render a skeleton while loading), and it disappears entirely once L09-F03 is fixed. Blast radius: the default route, every cold load.

190 {filteredBooks.map((book) => ( 191 void navigate(`/book/${book.id}`)} /> 192 ))} 193
194 ) : ( 195

findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. LibraryPage.tsx:18 destructures `{ books, addBook, getSummary }` and never takes `isLoading`, which the same object exposes (useLibrary.tsx:172). The ternary at :188 therefore reads the initial `[]` as 'no books' and renders 'Your library is quiet' (:200) plus an 'Add Your First Book' button (:212). The gate above is profile-only: App.tsx:12 returns a spinner for `useProfile().isLoading` and LibraryProvider mounts at App.tsx:32 only after that settles, so the library's own load window is entirely unguarded. useLibrary.tsx:20 initialises `isLoading` to true and reload() runs from a useEffect (:36-38) - i.e. after first paint - so the empty state is painted on 100% of cold loads for users with books, not intermittently. `categories` at :65 derives from the same array, so the topic filter row is empty in that window too. Medium is correct: user-visible wrong state on the default route, self-correcting within one IndexedDB read, no data impact.
findings.reachability: Every cold load of `/` for a profile with books: the first paint shows the zero-books empty state until `bookRepo.listByProfile` resolves.
findings.blastRadius: 1 consumer (the default route); the producer-side fix is shared with F069.
findings.suggestedPatch: LibraryPage.tsx:18 -> `const { books, isLoading, addBook, getSummary } = useLibrary();` and above :188 add `if (isLoading) return <Loader2 className="animate-spin" />;` (or a card skeleton grid) so the empty state is only reachable after the load settles. Risk: none; this mirrors BookDetailPage.tsx:19, which already gates on its own isLoading.

findings.title: The isLoading flag is only ever waited through, never asserted, so the false empty state on cold load is invisible
findings.description: `LibraryApi = ReturnType<typeof useLibraryState>` (useLibrary.tsx:185) is an untagged bag: `books: Book[]` and `isLoading: boolean` are independent fields, so `const { books } = useLibrary()` compiles cleanly while books is still the initial `[]` (useLibrary.tsx:19-20). Both test Probes (useLibrary.test.tsx:11-14 and goodreadsImport.test.tsx:17-20) render `api.isLoading ? 'loading' : books.length`, then `renderLibrary()` (line 26 here, line 32 there) waits past the loading window with `waitFor(...toHaveTextContent('0'))` and every subsequent assertion is against settled state. No test asserts isLoading === true at any point, and no test mounts a real consumer during the loading window. Of the seven production useLibrary() call sites, only useBookRoute.ts:10 reads isLoading -- LibraryPage.tsx:18, StatsPage.tsx:6, ProfilePage.tsx:9 and AppShell.tsx:27 destructure `{ books }` alone. LibraryPage.tsx:194-206 therefore renders the 'Your library is quiet' empty state on every cold load until IndexedDB resolves. A discriminated union ({ status: 'loading' } | { status: 'ready'; books: Book[] }) would turn each of those four call sites into a compile error. UNTESTED PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR: what any consumer renders before the first IndexedDB read completes.
findings.verifierNote: Every factual claim verifies; the severity and the anchor file do not. VERIFIED: `LibraryApi = ReturnType<typeof useLibraryState>` (useLibrary.tsx:185) is an untagged bag — `books` and `isLoading` are returned as independent fields at lines 171-172, initialised to `[]` and `true` at 19-20. Both Probes render `api.isLoading ? 'loading' : count` (useLibrary.test.tsx:13, goodreadsImport.test.tsx:19) and both `renderLibrary` helpers immediately wait past the loading window (useLibrary.test.tsx:26, goodreadsImport.test.tsx:32); a repo-wide grep confirms no test anywhere asserts `isLoading === true` for the library. Exactly 7 production `useLibrary()` call sites — AppShell.tsx:27, StatsPage.tsx:6, ProfilePage.tsx:9, LibraryPage.tsx:18, GoodreadsImport.tsx:13, BookDetailPage.tsx:13, useBookRoute.ts:10 — and only useBookRoute.ts:10,16 reads `isLoading`. The empty-state flash is real: App.tsx:12 gates on the PROFILE load only and then mounts `LibraryProvider` (App.tsx:32), so LibraryPage mounts with `books: []` and renders 'Your library is quiet' (LibraryPage.tsx:188 -> 194-216, heading at line 200) until the IndexedDB read in useLibrary.tsx:32 resolves. AMENDED TO MEDIUM: the consequence is a transient empty-state flash on cold load — no data loss, no crash, self-correcting within one IndexedDB round-trip. That is the spec's 'erodes confidence and refactor safety but isn't on a critical path'. Also, the finding is anchored to a test-file line; the defect lives in production source at useLibrary.tsx:170-183 (the untagged return) and its four unguarded consumers.
findings.reachability: Cold load with a populated library: open the app, pick a profile, land on /. LibraryPage renders 'Your library is quiet' with the 'Add Your First Book' CTA for one IndexedDB round-trip before the books appear. StatsPage.tsx:6 shows zeroes and ProfilePage.tsx:9 shows '0 Books in Library' for the same window. AppShell.tsx:58-78 is safe — it early-returns on `books.length === 0`.

The gap is invisible to the suite: both Probes render `isLoading ? 'loading' : count` (useLibrary.test.tsx:13, goodreadsImport.test.tsx:19) but both `renderLibrary` helpers immediately wait past the loading window (lines 26 and 32), and no test asserts `isLoading === true` or mounts a real consumer during it. findings.title: saveSummary is called by zero tests and the one summary test never asserts the denormalised Book fields
findings.description: Two gaps in one test. (a) `saveSummary` -- the function BookDetailPage.tsx:46 actually calls when an AI summary is generated -- is invoked by NO test in this file; every summary path here goes through `addBook(draft, { summary })` instead. (b) The one summary test asserts `summary?.oneSentenceTakeaway` read back from the summaries store (line 101) and `record.summaryId` (line 102), but never asserts the Book's own denormalised `oneSentenceTakeaway` or `readingTimeMinutes`. The `draft()` fixture (lines 30-39) hard-codes `readingTimeMinutes: 12` and omits `oneSentenceTakeaway` entirely -- legal only because types.ts:48 declares it optional -- so the persisted Book sits in the exact state the types.ts:41-48 doc comment says cannot exist: a book carrying a summaryId with no takeaway. Because the fixture pre-seeds a non-zero readingTimeMinutes, a 0 would never show either. Book is an untagged bag: `summaryId?`, `oneSentenceTakeaway?` and `readingTimeMinutes` are independent fields, so the compiler cannot require the denormalised pair when summaryId is present. useLibrary.tsx:82-83 writes only `{ ...book, summaryId: summary.id }` and never the pair, and BookCard.tsx:89/95 renders 'Not summarised yet' and '0 min read' for precisely that state. A discriminated Book (unsummarised | summarised with required takeaway + readingTime) would make the omission a compile error. UNTESTED PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR: the entire generate-summary-then-return-to-library flow.
findings.verifierNote: Pattern half-confirmed, reachability claim wrong, but the underlying union claim is corroborated by a site the discoverer missed. VERIFIED: `grep -rn saveSummary src/ --include=*.test.*` returns ZERO hits, so saveSummary genuinely has no test. useLibrary.test.tsx:84-103 asserts only the summaries-store read (line 101) and `record.summaryId` (line 102); the `draft()` fixture at lines 30-39 hard-codes `readingTimeMinutes: 12` (line 36) and omits `oneSentenceTakeaway`, legal per types.ts:48. REFUTED SUB-CLAIM: 'saveSummary is the function BookDetailPage.tsx:46 actually calls when an AI summary is generated' is false. Its only caller chain is BookDetail.tsx:186 `onSummaryUpdate(updated)` inside `handleMasterclassClick`, which returns early at BookDetail.tsx:183 `if (!summary) return;` — it is the deep-dive detailedSummary save, where `book.summaryId === summary.id` already holds, so the guard at useLibrary.tsx:82 `if (book && book.summaryId !== summary.id)` is false and the claimed impossible-state write at line 83 never fires. Initial summary creation goes through `addBook`, and BOTH production callers set the denormalised field: AddBookModal.tsx:72 `oneSentenceTakeaway: generated.summary.oneSentenceTakeaway` and LibraryPage.tsx:92 `{ ...book, oneSentenceTakeaway: summary.oneSentenceTakeaway }`. CORROBORATION the discoverer missed: src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:105-119 calls `books.create({...})` with `summaryId` (line 117) and `readingTimeMinutes` (line 115) but NO `oneSentenceTakeaway` key at all, while summaries.upsert at 122-132 writes the real takeaway to the summaries store. So every migrated legacy book compiles cleanly into exactly the state types.ts:41-48 says cannot exist, and BookCard.tsx:89 renders 'Not summarised yet' for it. migrate.test.ts:100 asserts only `expect(atomic?.summaryId).toBeTruthy()` and never checks the book's takeaway, so it is untested too. Severity amended down because the finding as filed is a test-coverage gap on one function with one caller, and the claimed production route is dead.
findings.reachability: As filed: not reachable — saveSummary's single caller (BookDetail.tsx:186, gated at :183) always has a matching summaryId so useLibrary.tsx:83 never runs. Reachable via the site the finding missed: any user with pre-IndexedDB localStorage data hits migrateLegacyData once (migrate.ts:80-151), and every migrated book then shows 'Not summarised yet' (BookCard.tsx:89) on the library grid despite having a stored summary.
findings.blastRadius: saveSummary: 1 production caller (BookDetailPage.tsx:46 <- BookDetail.tsx:186). The Book denormalisation invariant itself: 3 producers (migrate.ts:105, AddBookModal.tsx:69, LibraryPage.tsx:91) and 2 consumers (BookCard.tsx:89/95, StatsView via StatsPage.tsx:9).
findings.suggestedPatch:
Two-part, smallest first. (1) Fix the real bug — src/lib/storage/migrate.ts, inside the `books.create({...})` call at line 105, add one line next to `readingTimeMinutes`:

    readingTimeMinutes: legacy.readingTimeMinutes ?? 5,
+   oneSentenceTakeaway: legacy.oneSentenceTakeaway,

findings.title: useLibrary returns an untagged `{ books, isLoading }` bag, so `Book[]` cannot distinguish 'empty' from 'not loaded yet'
findings.description: The hook returns `books: Book[]` alongside a separate `isLoading: boolean`. Nothing in the type stops a consumer from reading `books` while `isLoading` is true, and during the whole first `bookRepo.listByProfile` round-trip `books` is `[]` -- an honest-looking empty library that is actually 'unknown'. Of the six consumers, only src/features/book/useBookRoute.ts:10 destructures `isLoading`, and it MUST (line 16 `if (isLoading) return;` is the only thing preventing a redirect off a valid `/book/:id` URL). The other four -- LibraryPage.tsx:18, StatsPage.tsx:6, ProfilePage.tsx:9, AppShell.tsx:27 -- take `books` alone and treat `[]` as authoritative. The compiler cannot flag any of them. ProfilePage.tsx:24 is the sharpest case: 'Delete everything' does `books.map((book) => removeBook(book.id))` and would silently delete only whatever subset happens to be in the stale array. Correct shape: a tagged union -- `{ status: 'loading' } | { status: 'ready'; books: Book[] }` -- which makes reading `books` in the loading state a compile error. Note the profile gate itself is correct and should not be flagged: `reload` waits on `profileLoading` (lines 22-25) and App.tsx:12/22 does not even mount `LibraryProvider` until the profile has settled and is non-null. Blast radius: six call sites, all of the library, stats, profile and book routes.

findings.title: The feature's entire public contract is inferred: `LibraryApi = ReturnType<typeof useLibraryState>`
findings.description: `useLibraryState` is module-private and carries no return type annotation; `LibraryApi` is derived from it with `ReturnType<>`, and `useLibrary(): LibraryApi` therefore has an annotation that is just an alias for 'whatever the implementation currently happens to return'. Nothing declares what this module promises. An incidental change inside any of the ten `useCallback`s -- a widened parameter, a narrowed return, a renamed key in the returned object literal -- silently rewrites the feature's public API, and TypeScript reports the breakage at the six consumer sites rather than at the source. There is no interface to diff a PR against and no place to document the contract. The repo already has the idiomatic fix one folder over: src/features/profile/ProfileContext.tsx:9-18 declares `interface ProfileContextValue` explicitly and annotates `useProfile(): ProfileContextValue`. `LibraryProvider` (line 193) likewise has no return annotation. Blast radius: six app call sites (AppShell.tsx:27, LibraryPage.tsx:18, StatsPage.tsx:6, ProfilePage.tsx:9, BookDetailPage.tsx:13, useBookRoute.ts:10, GoodreadsImport.tsx:13) plus two test files that re-derive `ReturnType<typeof useLibrary>`.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed exactly: useLibrary.tsx:17 `function useLibraryState()` carries no return annotation, :185 is `export type LibraryApi = ReturnType<typeof useLibraryState>;`, and :198 `export function useLibrary(): LibraryApi` is an annotation that resolves to 'whatever the implementation returns today'. The returned literal at :170-182 has 11 members, all inferred. The contrast the finding draws is real: ProfileContext.tsx:9-18 declares `interface ProfileContextValue` explicitly and annotates `useProfile(): ProfileContextValue` at :111. Blast radius recount: 7 non-test consumers, not six - AppShell.tsx:27, BookDetailPage.tsx:13, useBookRoute.ts:10, GoodreadsImport.tsx:13, LibraryPage.tsx:18, ProfilePage.tsx:9, StatsPage.tsx:6 - plus test files re-deriving `ReturnType<typeof useLibrary>` (goodreadsImport.test.tsx:15). The sub-claim about LibraryProvider (:193) lacking a return annotation is weak and I would not act on it: inferring the element type of a React component is idiomatic. Medium holds - pure refactor-safety erosion, no runtime consequence.
findings.reachability: No runtime path. Manifests on change: a narrowed return or renamed key inside any of the 11 members reports at the 7 consumers instead of at the source, with no interface to diff a PR against.
